# Māratajjanīya Sutta (MN 50 (PTS MN i 332))

**ID:** MN 50 (PTS MN i 332)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Māratajjanīya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 332
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

MN 50 shares extensive textual reuse with the *Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā* (Thag 20.1, vv. 1187–1208), which presents identical closing verses spoken by Moggallāna following his encounter with Māra [Nyanaponika et al. 2003; DharmaNexus]. Multiple cross-language parallels exist: three Chinese versions are preserved, including a sutra in the *Madhyama-āgama* (MĀ 131, T 26) and two independent translations, the *Mo raoluan jing* (T 66) and the *Bimo shi mulian jing* (T 67, ca. 250 CE) [Bingenheimer; DharmaNexus]. Parallel Sanskrit fragments are cataloged as SF 279 and SHT sutta 42 [DharmaNexus]. A comparative detail noted between versions is that while the *Madhyama-āgama* parallel depicts laypeople spreading their hair on the ground out of respect instigated by Māra, MN 50 lacks this specific motif [Anālayo].

- Full parallels: MA 131 降魔; SHT Sutta 42; T 66 魔嬈亂; T 67 弊魔試目連
- Passage-level parallels: Thag 20.1 Mahāmoggallānattheragāthā
- Resembling parallels: SF 279 Māratajjanīya
